sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Dovid's response to Hashem teaches that the essential point beyond general and particular is learned from Hashem, and this point connects to details in two ways: from details upward to the point, and from the point downward to details.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what is brought in Midrash Tehillim on the verse,
"One thing I asked of Hashem..."
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Dovid,
"At first you say, 'One thing I asked'
'that I dwell in the House of Hashem,' and afterwards you ask several things: 'to behold the pleasantness of Hashem' and 'to visit His Sanctuary,' etc."
And Dovid answered, "From You I learned:
At first You did not come upon me

except with one thing, as it is said, 'And now, Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you but to fear,' and afterwards You opened upon us many commandments, as it is said, 'to walk in all His ways and to cleave to Him,' etc."
And it needs to be understood,
for seemingly Dovid's answer "From You I learned" does not resolve the statement "One thing I asked,"
but rather it says that the question is about the Holy One, blessed be He,
that at first He says "but to fear" and afterwards He opened with many commandments.
And the Maggid explained,
that Dovid requested only one thing alone,
for the detailed matters
("to behold the pleasantness of Hashem" etc.)
are branches of "that I dwell in the House of Hashem."
And similarly regarding "What does Hashem your G-d ask of you but to fear,"
the detailed matters
("to walk in all His ways" etc.)
are branches of "to fear Hashem your G-d."
But,
according to this, it needs to be understood from the other side,
behold this matter
(that there are general matters from which many details branch)
is understood simply,
and why is it necessary to learn this from the Holy One, blessed be He?
And the point of the explanation in this is,
that the intention here in "one thing alone" is the essential point that is above general and details.
For this is what Dovid said, "One thing I asked,"
"One" is Yechidah,
the intrinsically singular,
that is not in the category of division into details
(as is known the distinction between Yachid and Echad).
And similarly regarding "to fear Hashem,"
for the explanation of "to fear Hashem"
(for the word "et" indicates something that is only secondary)
is that he has no existence of his own at all,
and his entire matter is only that he is secondary and nullified to Hashem.
And also according to what is explained in Tanya,
that "What does Hashem your G-d ask of you but to fear Hashem your G-d" refers to lower fear,
behold it is known,
that all the levels of fear are related to each other.
And also the self-nullification of lower fear is from the essence of the soul.
And as is known the distinction between fear and love,
that love, because it is a state of existence, is from the revelations of the soul,
and fear, because it is self-nullification, is from the essence of the soul.
And this is "From You I learned,"
for in order to connect the details with the essential point that is above general and details,
there is need for learning and empowerment from the Holy One, blessed be He.
And the connection of the essential point with the details is in two ways.
First,
in a manner from below to above,
that through the details one reaches the point.
And as it is written,
"And Hashem commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear Hashem,"
that through the fulfillment of the commandments
(the 613 particular commandments)
one comes to fear Hashem.
And second,
in a manner from above to below,
that from the point details are drawn and branch forth,
and in a manner that even after the details have been drawn,
the essential point that is above the source of the details shines within them.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The word "Mah" signifies essential self-nullification from the soul's essence, from which all details branch, and this nullification is higher than the nullification of fear which is still within the category of soul revelations.

translations.translation: And based on this, we can explain what they said, "Do not read 'Mah' but rather 'Me'ah,'
"Mah" is self-nullification, like "and we are what (mah)"
[And it can be said,
that this is that the term "Mah" indicates the smallness of the thing
(as above in section 2),
which is similar to what is said, "You are the smallest of all the nations," that they make themselves small],
and it is the essential self-nullification that is from the essence of the soul.
And the explanation of "What (Mah) does Hashem your G-d ask of you" is that Hashem your G-d asks of you the self-nullification of Mah.
And from this self-nullification all the details enumerated later in the verse branch forth,
including also "to fear Hashem."
For despite the fact that also the self-nullification of fear is from the essence of the soul,
and this self-nullification is the essential point from which the subsequent details branch
("to walk in all His ways" etc.),
nevertheless,
since the self-nullification is in the form of fear,
whose matter is
(like all the emotions)
the feeling that he is afraid,
it is included in the revelations of the soul,
but the self-nullification of Mah is essential self-nullification.
Like the self-nullification of mesirus nefesh
that is in every Jew,
from the Mah within him,
which is above all the faculties including even the faculty of will,
for that he gives his life is not from his will but because he cannot be separated, G-d forbid, from His Oneness.
And this is "What (Mah) Hashem your G-d,"
that the self-nullification of Mah is because Hashem
(He)
is your G-d, your strength and vitality.
For since Divinity is his vitality,
it is not applicable at all that he should be separated, G-d forbid, from Divinity.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The self-nullification of Mah is inherently concealed, and it is revealed through the service of the details (Me'ah), so that the revelation of Mah also permeates the particular faculties.

translations.translation: But,
the self-nullification of Mah that exists in every Jew is in concealment.
And this concealment is not only because of the animal soul that conceals and hides it,
but also from its own side it is hidden,
because it is above revelation.
And in order for it to be revealed,
about this they said, "Do not read 'Mah' but rather 'Me'ah.'
For Mah and Me'ah are two extremes.
Mah is an essential point that is above the category of details,
and Me'ah is a multitude of details up to the greatest multiplicity.
And in the soul of man, it is the ten faculties, each of which is comprised of ten.
And through the service in the particular faculties
(Me'ah),
the point of Mah is aroused and revealed.
And this is "Do not read 'Mah' but rather 'Me'ah,'
for Mah from its own side is above revelation – "Do not read"
(reading is revelation),
and its revelation is through the service of Me'ah.
And moreover,
the revelation of Mah
(that is brought about through the service of Me'ah)
is in a general manner and is also felt in the particular faculties.
And it can be said that this too is hinted at in "Do not read 'Mah' but rather 'Me'ah,'
for when the revelation of Mah is only in a general way,
then,
the revelation is only regarding the Mah
(that was initially in concealment and afterwards was revealed from its concealment),
and this is "Do not read 'Mah' but rather 'Me'ah,'
that the reading and revelation of Mah needs to be not only regarding the Mah but also in the particular faculties,
Me'ah.
